articles.title: Stock market today: BSE Sensex jumps 600 points, NSE Nifty50 trades above 22,550 mark
articles.full_text: Rupee remained under pressure against the US dollar in early trade on Monday, hovering around the crucial 96-per-dollar level amid elevated crude oil prices and sustained foreign fund outflows. The currency opened at 96.20 at the interbank foreign exchange market and slipped to 96.26 against the US dollar, down 1 paisa from its previous close. Forex traders said periodic intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) helped contain excessive intraday volatility and prevented sharper losses, although elevated import bills and continued strength in the US dollar kept investor sentiment under pressure. Rupee closed the holiday-shortened week at 96.3150 on Thursday, its weakest level in two months. The currency’s performance is being closely linked to the RBI’s upcoming monetary policy decision and the continued elevation in oil prices amid the Iran war. Over the weekend, signs of easing volatility in bond and currency markets provided some relief to investors, while US nonfarm payrolls data dented expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in the month. The RBI is set to announce its policy decision on Wednesday, with nearly 60 per cent of economists polled by Reuters expecting a 25-basis-point hike. Goldman Sachs economists also expected the RBI to raise rates. Stock market today: Top stocks to buy on October 5 Global bond yields are another important factor for market sentiment and risk appetite. Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, said that a moderation in US Treasury yields could ease pressure on emerging-market assets and create a more constructive environment for foreign flows. Conversely, a further rise in yields could increase the relative appeal of US assets and encourage continued portfolio reallocation away from emerging markets. Rising global bond yields had already been among the factors weighing on Indian equities, alongside foreign selling, rupee weakness and elevated crude prices. The direction of global yields therefore remains an important variable for the broader market environment. Oil prices found marginal relief as additional crude entered the market, with higher Middle Eastern shipments and the Group of Seven’s decision to release oil from emergency reserves easing some concerns over global energy supplies. The measures helped offset worries about possible further damage to energy infrastructure in the Gulf amid the Iran war. Brent crude was trading at $101.70, down 0.54 per cent, while WTI crude fell 0.92 per cent to $90.27. The G7 agreement covers the release of 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products, including diesel and crude, from emergency stocks. The countries have also pledged not to impose energy export restrictions. Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, described crude oil as the most immediate macroeconomic concern, citing pressure from Brent trading above $100 a barrel and continued geopolitical uncertainty. RBI’s interest rate decision, TCS’ earnings, crude oil prices and global bond yields are expected to be important factors determining stock market movement. Analysts have also pointed to macroeconomic data announcements and foreign investors’ trading activity as factors that could guide market trends. Ajit Mishra, SVP–Research at Religare Broking, said that the RBI monetary policy meeting would be closely watched, with its policy stance, inflation outlook and growth projections providing cues on the near-term trajectory of domestic interest rates and financial markets. The earnings season is also set to begin, with TCS and DMart among the key companies scheduled to announce their results. Asian markets traded mixed on Monday, with trading volumes subdued as holidays in China, South Korea and New South Wales in Australia kept some markets shut. Investors took cues from Wall Street’s Friday moves and shifting expectations around the Federal Reserve’s policy tightening cycle. Taiwan’s index gained 1,178.26 points, or 2.43%, while Japan’s Nikkei rose 1,640.66 points, or 2.4%. Malaysia’s index added 0.21% and Australia’s ASX 200 climbed 0.36%. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng bucked the trend, falling 0.29%. Nasdaq futures advanced 0.3 per cent and S&P 500 futures gained 0.1 per cent. EUROSTOXX 50 futures rose 0.3 per cent, while FTSE futures added 0.4 per cent. Among Asian markets, Taiwan and Japan posted gains of 2.43 per cent and 2.4 per cent respectively.

articles.title: Five Indiana engineering students built a 12-hour wearable that helps visually impaired users detect obstacles beyond a cane or guide dog
articles.description: Rose-Hulman students have developed a remarkable wearable device tailored for visually impaired individuals. This innovative headgear employs advanced sensors to identify surrounding obstacles, providing users with haptic feedback. With a remarkable twelve-hour battery life on a single charge, this device empowers users with greater independence. The project's goal is to enhance the day-to-day experiences of those with vision impairments.

articles.title: Sanjay Leela Bhansali, Alia Bhatt in talks to revive shelved Salman Khan starrer 'Inshallah'
articles.description: Sanjay Leela Bhansali and Alia Bhatt are reportedly discussing a revival of their shelved project Inshallah after 'Love and War.' Originally announced in 2019 with Salman Khan and Alia Bhatt, the film was stalled after creative differences between Bhansali and Salman. According to Mid-Day, the filmmaker and actor are now considering a substantially reworked version of the love story. Shah Rukh Khan was previously linked to the project, but casting decisions are yet to be finalised.

articles.title: FIRE BREAKS OUT at Talat Aziz's Juhu residence
articles.description: Talat Aziz, his wife Bina, and their two sons were hospitalized due to smoke inhalation from a fire. The incident occurred at their duplex apartment in Juhu late on Friday night. Emergency responders were able to control the blaze within an hour after arrival. As a result of the fire, several valuable possessions, including harmoniums and paintings, were lost.
